artworks.title: Phrixus and Helle Fleeing on the Golden Ram (fresco, MANN inv. 9478)
artworks.description: A Pompeian fresco now in the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli (inv. 9478) shows Phrixus clinging to the winged golden ram as his sister Helle slips toward the waves. The boy who will reach Colchis and dedicate the fleece is frozen mid-rescue — the flight that opens every Argonaut story. One of the canonical Roman images of the Athamas children's escape.

artworks.title: Phrixus and Helle (fresco from the Masseria di Cuomo, MANN inv. 8889)
artworks.description: Fourth-Style fresco from Pompeii's Masseria di Cuomo (MANN inv. 8889): Phrixus and Helle aboard Chrysomallus as they flee Ino's plot. The painter isolates the fatal crossing — Phrixus holds on; Helle will give her name to the Hellespont. Among the best-preserved Campanian treatments of the fleece's origin myth.

artworks.title: Apulian Volute Krater: Preparation for the Sacrifice of Phrixus and Helle (Darius Painter)
artworks.description: Monumental Apulian red-figure volute krater in Berlin (Antikensammlung inv. 1984.41): Athamas prepares to sacrifice Phrixus and Helle — the crisis from which the golden ram snatches the boy toward Colchis. South Italian vase painting stages Phrixus as the threatened heir whose rescue seeds the Golden Fleece.

artworks.title: Phrixus and Helle Crossing the Dardanelles (mosaic, Villa of San Marco, Stabiae)
artworks.description: Roman mosaic from the Villa of San Marco at Stabiae: Phrixus and Helle ride the golden ram across the strait that will take her name. Floor decoration turns the boy's escape into domestic spectacle — the same voyage that ends with Phrixus' welcome in Colchis and the fleece hung in Ares' grove.

artworks.title: Relief of Phrixos on the Golden Ram (Melian terracotta plaque, MET 12.229.20)
artworks.description: Melian terracotta relief in the Metropolitan Museum (Rogers Fund, 1912; inv. 12.229.20): Phrixus alone on the ram, carried over the sea toward Colchis. Classical plaque sculpture isolates the boy-hero of the fleece's origin — no Helle in frame, only the flight that leaves the Golden Fleece for Jason.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Harryhausen's voyage still begins with Phrixus' fleece: the golden ram's hide in Colchis is the prize whose origin story is the boy who fled Athamas on its back.

popCulture.title: Golden Fleece
popCulture.description: The fleece of the ram that saved Phrixus and Helle became the Argonauts' goal — his escape from the altar turned into the most famous quest-object in Greek myth.

popCulture.title: Phrixus
popCulture.description: The son of Athamas who rode the golden ram to Colchis — and left its fleece for Jason — remains the first chapter of every Argonautica.
